input.quote: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides termination only for material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and specific Vendor failures (9.3); there is no termination-for-convenience right for either Party, and Section 8.1 commits us to a three-year term with 180 days' non-renewal notice per Order Form (8.2). Under the playbook, the absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation. We inserted a new 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees (consistent with the existing refund mechanic in 10.2) and confirming Vendor has no mid-term convenience right. No early-termination or wind-down charge exists in Sections 7 or 10, so no penalty language needed deletion.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination charge, or other liability, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees covering the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on thirty days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, as the three-year term otherwise locks us in with no exit. Our fallback is 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.
proposal.summary: Insert Customer termination for convenience (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund) and confirm no Vendor convenience right.
